examples: We've got a new flat-screen telly.

senses.definition: (US, Canada, chiefly MTE, slang) A hotel or motel.
examples: I'm staying at the telly this weekend.

senses.definition: (informal, chiefly of a literary work) Inclined to telling (by explicitly stating facts), instead of showing (by conveying an impression so that events are described in the narrative).

quotes.text:
I think my problem with it is that it's
a) a little "telly" not "showy" in comparison to the rest […]
quotes.reference: 1999 November 21, sophie, “Squealer : first revision”, in alt.arts.poetry.comments (Usenet):

quotes.text: There's a way to make this more showy and less telly. It's like you're in a hurry to get on with the rest of the story.
quotes.reference: 2003 September 19, Patrick Null, “Failed Sept Challenge? (1409 words)”, in alt.fiction.original (Usenet):

quotes.text: story is too, too telly; need at least 3 showy scenes to improve showing:telling ratio

quotes.text: Six of Crows is very telly and little showy. You are constantly getting info dumps and mini-flashbacks to the characters past.
quotes.reference: 2016 February 12, Kelly, “Six of Crows by Leigh Bardugo”, in Diva Booknerd, archived from the original on 18 Jul 2024:

quotes.text: The only other objection I have—and again, it’s minor—is that the very last chapter feels very “telly” and rushed. I get why, but a smoother exit would have really made an otherwise wonderful book almost perfect.
quotes.reference: 2019 May 26, Chautona Havig, “This Book Gives New Meaning to “The Romance of the Rails””, in Chautona.com, archived from the original on 18 Jul 2024:

quotes.text: Lee’s style of narration reads like an old-style fairy tale to an extent—it’s very telly, if that makes any sense. We get descriptions of character actions and we’re told about character motives as filtered through the third-person narrator, but we don’t actually get to read these characters’ thoughts.
quotes.reference: 2022 October 10, Brian Collins, “Short Story Review: “Bite-Me-Not or, Fleur de Fleu” by Tanith Lee”, in Science Fiction & Fantasy Remembrance, archived from the original on 18 Jul 2024:

quotes.text: The ending felt rushed to me, and I wish it would have been more showy and less telly.
